parsed.explanation: Below the 0.35 tier because a criminal statute is documented as actually used against trans people: Article 489 (6 months–3 years) applied on the basis of gender expression, with wide police discretion and hundreds charged; plus morality charges, police forcing a trans woman to display her genitals (2024), and officers handcuffing/filming a cross-dresser and posting his ID online (2019) — state-actor abuse with no recourse (no anti-discrimination law, LGBT organisations blocked, minister calling homosexuals 'trash', hostile curriculum, 21% acceptance). Aggravating: a documented beating of a trans woman and reported significant risk of violence on public identification. Not the 0.15 tier: no trans-specific offence, no documented sweeps, custody or ward-placement pattern, no established custodial sexual violence, and one assault was prosecuted. Visitor-specific care, custody and ward practice are undocumented — open questions, not safety. Extrapolating the enforced criminal-plus-police-abuse regime: 0.24.
